spec: Technical Specification v0.6.0 §K.8a (D-46), §I.2 rule 11a, §I.3 preservation PR-1–PR-6
meaning: One documented deployment ignore list, applied consistently: the build never packages a matching path, and the site preserves a matching path that already exists inside a managed component directory. It is not .gitignore, and .gitignore is not consulted.
scope: Patterns match paths relative to each managed component directory (plugins/{slug}/ or themes/{slug}/). Everything outside the managed scope is never touched regardless of this list.

rules: A pattern without a slash (apart from a trailing one) matches a file or directory name at any depth.
A pattern with a slash elsewhere is anchored at the component root; a leading slash is allowed and equivalent.
A trailing slash matches a directory and everything under it, never a file of that name.
A path below a matched directory is excluded.

* matches any run of characters except /; ? matches one character except /; a ** segment matches zero or more segments, and one or more when it ends the pattern (docs/** excludes everything inside docs, not docs itself).

Matching is byte-wise and case-sensitive over the UTF-8 bytes of the path: ? matches exactly one byte and * a run of bytes, so ? never matches a multi-byte character (use * for names with non-ASCII characters). Patterns themselves are ASCII.

Matching cost is bounded by pattern bytes × path bytes: every implementation is a dynamic programme at both levels — over (pattern segment, path segment) for the anchored walk and over (pattern byte, segment byte) inside a segment — with no regular expression and no backtracking, so repeated ** segments and repeated * or ? wildcards are safe.
refused: empty patterns, empty segments, . or .. segments
** inside a segment (only a whole ** segment)
a ** segment followed by the trailing slash
patterns without any literal character, which would match everything

canonical_form: The fixed patterns and the enabled additions, deduplicated, sorted by bytes, one per line, each line LF-terminated, UTF-8, no comments and no blank lines. exclusions_sha256 is the SHA-256 of these bytes; the site serves the text in GET /site, the gate passes it to the build, the release request echoes the hash, and a mismatch is EXCLUSIONS_STALE.

rejected_for_safety.note: Not exclusions. The archive validator refuses these on the site and in CI (Technical Specification §I.2 rule 11); they are listed here so the setup screen can show them under "Always refused".
